questions.question: OP-01/O47: D65 lets an O2 replace/delete fail on Local/Windows while O1 holds a stream open. D10 says the state after any OP-01 call is what 'the environment alone leaves', D20 that a cancelled read 'changes nothing (D10)', D24 that each call behaves 'as if issued alone' (O8 unamended). How do D10 and D24 state the deviation?

options.label: Scoped exception (Recommended)
options.description: D10 and D24 gain: where D43's Overlapping mutation deviation is declared, an open OP-01 read may make an overlapping API mutation of that item fail, leaving the state as before that mutation; nothing else. D20's 'changes nothing' and O8 cite it. Source: D65, D43 (AX-15 forbids an undeclared deviation).

options.label: Recast O2's failure
options.description: D10 unchanged: O2's failed mutation counts as the environment's outcome, not OP-01's effect; D24 alone gains the exception. Leaves a reader of D10 unaware that a read can block a write.

options.label: Withdraw deviation
options.description: Reverse D65: Local on Windows opens reads with FILE_SHARE_DELETE so mutations succeed; D10/D24 stand. Rests on unrun delete-pending/rename behaviour D65 avoided.

questions.question: OP-01/O48: D43 has configuration select a declaration where one backend serves differing services; D64 rejected configuration and declared 'Local on a network file system, across hosts, is eventual', static. With no probe and no config, a Local store must declare eventual everywhere (penalising local disks) or strong (undeclared on NFS). Which?

options.label: Conditioned declaration (Recommended)
options.description: D43 admits a static declaration conditioned on a stated property of the store's location (here: a network file system shared across hosts). The caller knows the condition; nothing probes or configures. O12 amended. Ground precedent: profile 052's per-platform Local columns and SFTP's 'the server's file system' cells.

options.label: Config, default strong
options.description: Local gains a configuration flag for shared network file systems; unset means strong. D43's 'unnamed takes the deviations' narrowed to services. An NFS user who forgets the flag gets an undeclared deviation.

options.label: Config, default eventual
options.description: Same flag, unset means eventual (D43's rule as written). Every local-disk store declares eventual unless configured, against D64's 'without penalising local disks'.

options.label: Eventual always
options.description: Local declares eventual unconditionally; no condition, no config. Simple, but OP-18 then reports a weaker guarantee for every Local store.

questions.question: OP-01/O63: D64 and D65 name Local only, though D14 declared SFTP's server-side file system for termination. An SFTP server on Windows would refuse rename/remove of a file open in another session; two SFTP servers on one NFS export would show D64's staleness. Does SFTP declare these deviations?

options.label: Both, conditioned (Recommended)
options.description: SFTP declares Overlapping mutation where the server runs on Windows and Read-after-write eventual where the server's file system is a network one shared across hosts: profile 052's 'the server's file system' convention, as D14 did. Not run.

options.label: Both, unconditionally
options.description: SFTP declares both deviations for every server. Never undeclared, but OP-18 reports weaker guarantees for every Linux SFTP server.

options.label: Neither
options.description: SFTP keeps the normal values; a Windows or NFS-backed server deviates undeclared, which AX-15's check forbids.

OP-01/O49 (category): an archive-tier move fits both E15 (unreadable in place) and E16 (system property changed). D47: a resume under E15 fails 'not readable'; D62: on Azure any property change also fails a resume 'changed'. Which category does a stream's resume surface after a tier move, and are the rows made disjoint?

options.label: Disjoint, unspecified (Recommended)
options.description: E16 excludes E15's moves (rows disjoint). Under E15, where D62's deviation is declared (Azure), a resume fails not readable or changed, which one unspecified (F3); elsewhere not readable (D47). The library makes no extra request to tell them apart. Source: D47, D62, axes.md F3.

options.label: Disjoint, always not readable
options.description: Rows disjoint; after a 412 on Azure the library makes a further request to learn whether the item is archived and reports not readable. One category, at an extra request on the failure path (NP2).

options.label: Overlap kept, changed wins
options.description: E15 and E16 both apply; where the pin token changes, changed is reported. D47 narrowed to backends whose token survives a tier move. Callers re-read and then meet not readable.

questions.question: OP-01/O49 (reason): D61's recommendation says 'changed claims a change the library cannot know of' and its check 'changed still means a change the backend proved'. Under D62's Azure deviation, changed fires on a token change while the content is the open's. How does D61 read?

options.label: Token, not content (Recommended)
options.description: D61's check reads: changed means the backend's pin token no longer matches (D62), which the backend proved; under D62's deviation the content may be the open's. Its outcome stands. Source: D62's 'Changed means the backend's pin token no longer matches'.

options.label: Leave D61
options.description: D61's text stands; D62 is read as overriding it. A reader of D61 alone keeps the false claim.

questions.question: OP-01/O54 (O2 metadata): no Environment row covers O2 changing an item's metadata through OP-20 (optional entry). E16 is O3's; D62's changed row has no O2 member, though on Azure such a change would fail a resume changed (not run). How is it covered?

options.label: New row E18 (Recommended)
options.description: E18: O2 changes an item's metadata or system properties through the API (OP-20, where offered). Exposed at s3 through a new request; outcomes as E16's: changed only where D62's deviation is declared, else nothing. D62's changed row gains E18. Source: D62, catalogue OP-20.

options.label: Widen E1
options.description: E1 'creates or replaces an item' is read to include an OP-20 metadata change. One row fewer, but every decision citing E1 (D21, D23) then covers metadata changes it never considered.

options.label: Out of scope
options.description: OP-20 is optional and its session decides; OP-01 lists no row. A Azure resume after an OP-20 change then fails with no Environment row admitting it.

questions.question: OP-01/O54 (O3 create): no row covers O3 creating an item at an absent key (E3 'replaces', E5 'deletes'), yet D63's and D66's scenarios use it and D63 covers 'an O3 change of E3 or E5' only. How is it covered?

options.label: New row E19 (Recommended)
options.description: E19: O3 creates an item at an absent key as one step (a PUT of a new object, a rename onto a free name). Exposed at s2 and s3 as E3; D25's set (E3, E5) and D63's real-time order gain E19. Source: D63, D66 scenarios.

options.label: Widen E3
options.description: E3 is read as 'creates or replaces'. Every decision citing E3 covers creation implicitly; no new row, less explicit for the spec.

OP-01/O50 (D4, D34): D67 amends D9 and D19 only. D4 still says 'every other pre-state is a failure' though E17 admits content, and D34's table has no E17 row although its check says every Environment row has a category. How are D4 and D34 amended?

options.label: Amend both (Recommended)
options.description: D4 reads: outside E17 (D67), OP-01 is meaningful exactly for Found(e, item). D34 gains a row 'E17, a key at or above k | not found or not an item, or success with the object at k (D67)', builtins as those rows. Source: D67, D4, D34's check.

options.label: D34 only
options.description: D34 gains the E17 row; D4 left, read as describing the state spec 051 admits. D4's 'every other pre-state is a failure' then stays literally false under E17.

questions.question: OP-01/O50 (stream): D67 exposes E17 at s2 and s3, its outcomes 'content, not found, not an item', which D45 bars from a stream read. If O3 creates `a.txt/b` while O1 streams `a.txt`, the object at `a.txt` is unchanged. What does a stream read surface under E17?

options.label: s2 only, stream goes on (Recommended)
options.description: D67's exposure narrows to s2 (classification, including a whole read's one request). A stream opened before or during E17 continues under D22: the object at k is pinned, so a read meets nothing of E17's own. D45 unchanged. Source: D22, D45.

options.label: Keep s3, add to D45
options.description: A stream read may fail not found or not an item under E17; D45's list widens. Claims an outcome no backend request produces for a pinned object.

questions.question: OP-01/O50 (scope): D67's Decision says 'while a key at or above k is in that state', its dialog option said 'that key'. With objects `a` and `a/b/c`, reading `a/b/c` hits BlockedByItem(a) yet a GET returns content. Which scope?

options.label: At or above k (Recommended)
options.description: Keep D67's Decision: the unspecified outcome holds while k or any ancestor key is both item and folder. Needed for D67's own scenario (`a.txt/b` lies below the dual key `a.txt`). Source: D67's scenario, KEY-013.

options.label: Exactly k
options.description: Only k itself in E17's state. Then reading `a.txt/b` falls under D9, which says not found while S3 returns content: an outcome no clause admits.

questions.question: OP-01/O50 (variation): E17 arises on flat object stores only, the shape of D43's 'O3 in-place modification' point (cannot arise / arises with weaker rights). D76's five points name none for E17. Is it a variation point?

options.label: Sixth point (Recommended)
options.description: D43 gains 'Dual key (E17)': normal value cannot arise (file systems, hierarchical namespaces); declared deviation arises with D67's unspecified outcome (flat object stores). O13 and D76 count six. OP-18 then tells a caller whether its store can be in that state. Source: D43's O3 in-place row.

options.label: No point
options.description: D67's outcome holds wherever E17 arises; whether it can arise is not exposed. O3 in-place modification is then the only point of that shape, an inconsistency.

options.label: Sixth point (Recommended)

options.description: D67's outcome holds wherever E17 arises; whether it can arise is not exposed. O3 in-place modification is then the only point of that shape, an inconsistency.
options.label: No point

questions.question: OP-01/O50 (variation): E17 arises on flat object stores only, the shape of D43's 'O3 in-place modification' point (cannot arise / arises with weaker rights). D76's five points name none for E17. Is it a variation point?

OP-01/O51 (Closed): D80 puts argument checks first 'in every state but Closed', leaving a caller error on a Closed stream undecided. On a closed io.BufferedReader, read('x') raises TypeError and read(2) ValueError (CPython 3.13.17, per the review). Which comes first on a Closed stream?

options.label: Arguments first (Recommended)
options.description: One rule for every state, Closed included: a caller error is raised first, then a valid call raises ValueError (D15). Matches io, whose contract D70 adopts, and D80's adopted option 'one rule for every state'.

options.label: Closed first
options.description: On a Closed stream every call but close raises ValueError whatever its arguments. Simpler to state, but unlike io: read('x') on a closed file raises TypeError there.

questions.question: OP-01/O51 (Failed): D80 says 'a valid call on a Failed stream raises the failure again (D52)', which literally covers close(), tell(), readable() and seekable() too, while D16/D18 have close release. Which calls re-raise on a Failed stream?

options.label: Reads only (Recommended)
options.description: read, readinto, readline, read1, chunks and iteration re-raise (D52); close releases (D16, D18); tell returns bytes delivered, readable true, seekable false; seek/truncate/write raise io.UnsupportedOperation. D16, D18, D52 and D80 narrowed to reads. Source: D16's adopted 'close works', D18's close column, io.

options.label: All but close
options.description: Every method but close re-raises, tell and readable included. A Failed stream then answers no question about itself; no io precedent.

questions.question: OP-01/O58 (read1): D18's column lists `read`, `readinto`, `readline`, chunks, but not `read1`, which D70 adds as drawing 'from the one position'. Where does read1 go in D18's table?

options.label: Into that column (Recommended)
options.description: D18's first column reads `read`, `readinto`, `readline`, `read1`, chunks, iteration: every reading method shares one row of transitions. Source: D70, D78.

options.label: A column of its own
options.description: read1 gets its own column with the same cells. More table, no behavioural difference.

questions.question: OP-01/O58 (async): D69's adopted option read 'Same methods, awaited'; its Decision added, unasked, that tell/readable/seekable stay plain methods, and seek/truncate/write are in neither list. In the async form, which methods are coroutines?

options.label: All awaited (Recommended)
options.description: Every method of the sync object is a coroutine in the async one, tell, readable, seekable, seek, truncate and write included (the last three raising io.UnsupportedOperation when awaited). D69's adopted wording; prior art aiofiles and anyio AsyncFile. D69's plain-methods sentence withdrawn.

options.label: Plain if no request
options.description: Only methods that may make a request are coroutines (read, readinto, readline, read1, close); tell, readable, seekable, seek, truncate, write plain. Fewer awaits, but parity is no longer method by method.
